deep.reconstruction:
This is a printed page from an elementary German arithmetic textbook (p. 30). Gauss's hand appears only in two small corrections and in the right-margin numbers. The margin figures continue onto the next page ('Rechnung bei 60°').

Printed text, top (end of §83, decimal conversion of fractions). A fraction p/q has a terminating decimal exactly when the reduced denominator divides a power of ten. Otherwise the decimal is only an approximation, with an error that can be made arbitrarily small. Example: 2/3 - 0.666666 = (2/3)*10^-6. The print gives the remaining error as a small fraction over 1000000.

§84, division with decimals.
(1) Pad dividend and divisor with zeros to the same number of decimal places. Both can then be treated as integers, since a/b = (a*10^k)/(b*10^k).
(2) For more digits, multiply the dividend by 10^m, i.e. append m zeros. Divide as integers, then point off m digits in the quotient: a/b = 10^-m * (a*10^m)/b.

Worked long division, 19000 / 563 (i.e. 1.9/563):
- 1900 - 3*563 = 1900 - 1689 = 211
- 2110 - 1689 = 421
- 4210 - 7*563 = 4210 - 3941 = 269
- 2690 - 4*563 = 2690 - 2252 = 438
So the quotient is 0.003374... with remainder 438.

Side examples:
- 194.235/563 = 194235/563000 = 0.345, because 563*345 = 194235.
- 194235/5.63 = 19423500/563 = 34500.
- 1942.35/0.563 = 1942350/563 = 3450.
- 1.9/563 = 19/5630 = 0.003374...

§85: to divide named (dimensioned) quantities of the same kind, reduce everything to the smallest unit first. §86: division with letters (algebraic division).

Handwritten corrections:
- The misprinted numerator '149235' is corrected to '194235' (a '94' is written above it).
- In §86 the cross-reference '§.14' is changed to '§.15'.

Right-margin numbers. Most are cropped. The legible block matches the next page and is a common-logarithm computation of log10(M*pi/18), where M = log10(e) = 0.4342945 (the label reads '1/18 pi · 0,434'). In 10-shifted characteristics:
- log10 M = 9.6377843 - 10
- log10 pi = 0.4971499
- sum = 0.1349342 (i.e. 10.1349342 - 10)
- log10 18 = 1.2552725
- difference = 8.8796617 - 10

So M*pi/18 ≈ 0.07580. This is the Briggsian equivalent of a 10° arc, i.e. log10(e^(pi/18)); the value 0.0757987 appears on the next page. The upper margin figures (0.87401..., 850..., 8532, 8654..., 865523...) are fragments of the series/difference computation shown in full on the next page, for 60°. They are too cropped to reconstruct here.
errors: The printed remainder 2/3 - 0.666666 should be (2/3)/1000000, about 6.67e-7. If the small numerator is read as '4' (4/1000000), the print is wrong. It may instead be a poorly printed 2/3, or the text may mean 4 more digits in some sense; the reading is uncertain.
Misprint 149235 for 194235 in the first side example; corrected by hand on the page.
Cross-reference §.14 corrected by hand to §.15 in §86.
The appeal to '§.81' for the error vanishing seems to point to §82 (the 1/∞ principle); §81 concerns the gcd of several numbers. Likely a wrong cross-reference in the print.

The printed small fraction after 'nur noch' is uncertain ('4/1000000' or possibly a smudged 2/3 over 1000000); the mathematically correct value is (2/3)/1000000.
